solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English constable is distinguished

parts.note: a special constable, or special, is a volunteer police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: A police constable from England is singled out as a person of distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPECIAL is a part-time volunteer constable in British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is an old-fashioned synonym for notable or exceptional, meaning set apart from the ordinary.

clue.text: Former shelter of some size

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: An old shelter of some considerable size.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the area or scale of something, its magnitude.

clue.text: To reach near-perfect stage of development, young animal took food

definitions.text: To reach near-perfect stage of development

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or seal
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A young animal eats, growing towards maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupa is the stage just before the imago, the 'perfect' adult insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects become pupae just before the adult imago form, the last step before maturity.

clue.text: Compel firm to visit A&E, for example, and church

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
A&E, the British accident and emergency department, is an emergency room or ER
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A company is ordered to visit the hospital casualty unit and a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's casualty department; the American equivalent is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone is to force them to act, a synonym of compel.

clue.text: Within reach entrance is bolted oddly

parts.note: access means a way in

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The entry door is strangely bolted, though it seemed easy to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd letters of 'is bolted': I, B, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Accessible means reachable or available, able to be got at.

clue.text: Show clearly First Lady going round in open car

indicators.note: the first lady's name goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of car is taken

explanation.surface: A president's wife tours in a convertible, making a public display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife but is EVE; 'open car' is the first letter of car, C, not a convertible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to make evident or plainly display a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Pretension of Ivan the Terrible wearing cape

indicators.note: wearing joins the cape on to the rearranged name
terrible treatment of the name Ivan mangles its letters

parts.note: ness is a word for a headland or cape

explanation.surface: The Russian tsar Ivan the Terrible shows off in a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Terrible' completes the tsar's title but signals an anagram of IVAN, giving VAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainness is conceit or self-importance, close to pretension.

clue.text: Beginning to develop 'ants' as in 'pants'

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so it tells us to mess up the letters before it

explanation.surface: A remark about ants getting into trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for bad or rubbish, a modern anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Naissant, from French for being born, means emerging or coming into existence.

clue.text: Elves' sin is convulsed in depravity

indicators.note: convulsed means shaken violently, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: The sin of some elves is shaking them in their wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Evilness is wickedness or moral corruption, the same as depravity.

clue.text: Put back small-change coin

indicators.note: back says the word Put is written in reverse order

parts.note: pence are the small coins of British currency

explanation.surface: Someone returns a little loose coin to its place.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is Put turned round by 'back'; a TUPPENCE is an old British twopenny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuppence is a British coin worth two pennies, so a type of coin.

clue.text: A toll, we hear, comprising two separate material parts

definitions.meaning: said aloud this sounds like atoll
a two-piece swimsuit made of a top and a bottom

explanation.surface: A road charge is overheard being split into two pieces of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works only by sound: 'a toll' spoken is 'atoll', and Bikini is a famous Pacific atoll.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece swimsuit and the Marshall Islands atoll share one name.

clue.text: Coat seen misshaped by a wallet

indicators.note: misshaped tells us the letters of the two words are bent into a new form

explanation.surface: A coat is seen to have been pushed out of shape by a wallet in its pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old name for a pocketbook used to hold banknotes.

clue.text: Complete agreement on university issue

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university
issue means offspring, here a son

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees about a matter concerning the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a topic, but in the sense of offspring it gives SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in total accord, all together as one.

clue.text: Correspondent at Crown Office event

parts.note: CO is short for Crown Office
an incident is an event or occurrence

explanation.surface: A news correspondent attends an event at the Crown Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondent' suggests a reporter but means matching or corresponding.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident means happening together or corresponding exactly, an adjectival sense of correspondent.

clue.text: Emulsion is sprayed on automobiles

indicators.note: sprayed suggests the letters are scattered about and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Emulsion paint is sprayed over some cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Limousines are large luxury cars, so a kind of automobile.

clue.text: Cruel and senseless to sing inside

indicators.note: inside says the singing word goes within the senseless word

parts.note: inane means senseless or silly
to hum is to sing with closed lips

explanation.surface: It is cruel and pointless to sing indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion, unkind or cruel.

clue.text: Made from, for example, seedless grapes whisked up (but not scrambled)

definitions.text: Made from, for example, seedless grapes whisked up (but not scrambled)

parts.words: Made from, for example, seedless grapes whisked up (but not scrambled)
parts.note: read 'for example, seedless' as eggs, sounded out from e.g. plus s: a dish of eggs beaten up but cooked flat rather than scrambled

explanation.walkthrough: The grapes are a red herring: the dish is made from beaten eggs, folded rather than scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked flat in a pan, unlike scrambled eggs.

clue.text: When at home whelp destroyed brood

parts.note: in means at home
a whelp is a cub, a young animal
ate can mean consumed or destroyed, as acid ate away the metal

explanation.surface: When a pup is at home it gets torn apart by the brood.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to sit on eggs to hatch them, which is what incubate means.

clue.text: Is this buffer-zone hers?

parts.note: the strip between two front lines is said to belong to nobody male, so the clue wonders whether it must belong to a woman

explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the phrase literally: land of no man, so perhaps a woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: The unoccupied strip between opposing armies' trenches is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Some bank a rand to achieve capital

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some deposit a South African rand at the bank to build up capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The rand is South Africa's currency, adding to the banking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: A couple of hundred ordinary Republican delegates begin to agree

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them

indicators.note: begin says the opening letter of delegates is the one needed

explanation.surface: A couple of hundred ordinary Republican delegates start to reach agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to be in agreement or harmony.

clue.text: Fed up with objective guard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word Fed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A guard who is fed up with his objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like the idiom but 'up' reverses FED to DEF in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect or guard against attack.

clue.text: Hesitation by lout sounding a vowel change

parts.note: um is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

indicators.note: sounding says we want a word that is pronounced like lout

parts.note: a lout is an oaf; laut, German for sound, is pronounced the same way

explanation.surface: A thug hesitates and a vowel in his speech shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUT, the German word for sound, is pronounced like 'lout'.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is a shift in vowel quality in Germanic languages, and the two-dot mark showing it.

clue.text: Highest point at which to fasten clean dressing

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten it

indicators.note: dressing suggests the letters of clean are prepared or arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A nurse pins a fresh bandage in place at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like a bandage but rearranges CLEAN to NACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the summit or peak, the topmost point of something.

clue.text: Authentic material

definitions.meaning: relevant, real and substantial, as opposed to theoretical

explanation.definitionFit: Actual means real or existing in fact, which covers both genuine and substantive.

clue.text: Not to mention the tale Noel fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters are built into something new

explanation.surface: A story Noel made up, not to mention others.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means much less or still less, used like the phrase not to mention.

clue.text: A side, one-by-one

definitions.meaning: a team in football or cricket fields this many players
the digit 1 set beside another 1 reads as 11

explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has eleven players, and two ones written side by side make the number.

clue.text: Tube station to which the pressman was abandoned

parts.note: Strand was a former London Underground station, later renamed Aldwych
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist was left at a London Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; Strand was the old name of its Aldwych station.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded means left helpless or abandoned with no means of getting away.
